## 2026-11-24 - supplier: individual type, one photo, editable code

User request (grill-me, 3 rounds): fix supplier CRUD — code from the code
numbering settings, types `Company / Government / Individual`, NPWP not
deleted (only optional), and one photo like a warehouse instead of a gallery.
Resolved: Individual is a `supplier_type` value (not a company-less PIC row),
NPWP stays untouched in the schema and the PO snapshot, code stays editable,
photo is a single `image_object_key`, list stays minimal.

**Backend (`src/app/supplier`)**

- `SUPPLIER_COMPANY_TYPES` + `supplier_type` check now
  `('company','government','individual')`; `contracts` enum widened.
- `companies.image_object_key text` (nullable). New
  `services/supplier-image.service.ts` (+ `SUPPLIER_IMAGE_SERVICE_TOKEN`,
  registered in `container.ts`): `PUT|DELETE /suppliers/companies/:id/image`
  behind `supplier:update`, multipart `file` → `storeDocumentImage` (WebP, 2 MB)
  → `documentImageUrl` presigned. `imageUrl` rides on the list, detail, create
  and update responses; bank masking still applies first.
- `SupplierService.updateCompany` upper-cases a new code and rejects one held
  by another live company (`SupplierCompanyCodeTakenError`); `createCompany`
  upper-cases a typed code. Previously a duplicate on update surfaced as a raw
  500 from the unique index.
- `ExportedSupplierService.getPurchaseSnapshot` unchanged: NPWP still travels
  into `procurement.purchase_orders.supplier_snapshot` (nothing dropped, no
  backfill).

**Migration** `20261124090000_erp0123_supplier_photo_individual_type`
(2 statements, inspected): `ADD COLUMN image_object_key text`; drop + recreate
`supplier_companies_type_check` with the third value. **Not applied** to any
database.

**Web admin**

- `lib/supplier-api.ts`: `SUPPLIER_TYPES` + `individual`, `imageUrl` and
  `createdAt` on the row type, `uploadSupplierImage` / `removeSupplierImage`,
  `updateSupplierPerson`; the request helper now only sets a JSON content type
  for string bodies (a `FormData` body keeps its own boundary).
- Form dialog: `ImageDropzone` single photo (uploaded right after the company
  write, create and edit), NPWP and legal name hidden for `individual` and
  cleared when switching type, "(Optional)" from the shared `FieldLabel`.
- List: photo thumbnail column, rest unchanged (photo, code, name, type,
  contact, status, actions).
- Detail: photo card (upload/replace/delete), village → province line under
  each address (`villageChainQueryOptions`), editable PIC, `createdAt`.

**Seed.** `database/seeders/seed/supplier.seeder.ts` (called after
`seedOrganizationRoles`): `DEV-SUP-CO`, `DEV-SUP-GOV`, `DEV-SUP-IND` anchored
by code, PIC + address for the first two; a second run inserts nothing.

**Verification**

- `bun docs/database/gen-logical-references.ts` → 189 refs; `validate-dbml.ts`
  → `OK` (196 tables, 153 refs, 0 cross-module, 0 timestamp gaps, 0 drizzle
  parity drift, 0 column parity drift).
- `bun run drizzle:generate` → the 2-statement migration above;
  `bunx --bun drizzle-kit check` → `Everything's fine`;
  `generate --explain` → `no_changes`.
- `apps/backend`: `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun test` **1459 pass / 0 fail**
  (new: upper-case on create, duplicate code on update, individual accepted,
  image signing/clearing/not-found).
- `apps/web-admin`: `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` clean.
- `packages/locales`: `bun test` 106 pass (parity + no dead keys, so every new
  key exists in `en` and `id` and is referenced).

## 2026-11-24 - dependabot PR #157: re-patch `@unplugin-pwa/core` 0.0.8 for Bun

`Docker Build Web Customer Portal` failed on PR #157 (`@vite-pwa/astro`
`2.0.3` -> `2.0.4`, which pulls `@unplugin-pwa/core`/`vite`/`inspector`
`0.0.7` -> `0.0.8`). Symptom, job `138373169544`:

```text
[ERROR] [@vite-pwa/astro-integration] An unhandled error occurred while
running the "astro:config:setup" hook
Export named 'findPackageJSON' not found in module 'node:module'.
error: script "build" exited with code 1
```

Cause: the `bun patch` in ERP-0107 is keyed by exact version
(`"@unplugin-pwa/core@0.0.7"`), so the bump silently dropped it and the
unpatched `0.0.8` went back to the static `findPackageJSON` import. Same
failure mode already recorded in `stack-compatibility.md`.

Fix: `patches/@unplugin-pwa%2Fcore@0.0.8.patch` (same hunk, retargeted; the
`0.0.7` patch and its `patchedDependencies` entry are gone) — only
`dist/resolve-inspector-dist.mjs` carries the import; all 30 `core` and 25
`vite` `0.0.8` `dist/*.mjs` files were scanned, no other hit.

Verified locally on `fix/dependabot-pwa-0-0-8` (based on the dependabot
commit `f9318f7e`):

- `bun install` -> patched file present in `node_modules/@unplugin-pwa/core/dist/resolve-inspector-dist.mjs`; `bun.lock` `patchedDependencies` now keyed `0.0.8`.
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile` -> `Checked 1394 installs across 1445 packages (no changes)`.
- `bun --bun run --cwd apps/web-customer-portal build` -> `[build] ✓ Completed in 12.53s` (was the CI failure point).
- `docs/database/` reviewed, unchanged (dependency-only change).

## 2026-11-24 - web-admin: organization role dropdown on the new-employee dialog

User request: `/hr/employees` "Karyawan baru" dialog had no role picker, while
`/admin/users` does. Backend already supported it — `POST
/human-resources/employees` accepts `organizationRoles` (`hr.contract.ts`),
validates it against the shared ladder (`employee.controller.ts`), and
`EmployeeInviteService` defaults to `['member']` when an organization is set —
so this was frontend-only. Invited employees silently always got `member`.

- `components/hr/employee-create-dialog.tsx`: `useGrantableOrgRoles(activeOrganizationId)`
  supplies the options (same ladder as the invitation dialog: no `owner`, no
  `admin`/`hr` above the caller's tier), `erpRoleLabel` renders them in the UI
  language, and the picked role is sent as `organizationRoles: [effectiveRole]`.
  The effective role is clamped at render (a role picked before the ladder
  loads is not trusted), and the field only renders when an active
  organization exists — without one the backend reads a role list as an org
  invite and rejects it, so `organizationRoles` stays `undefined`.
- Locales en/id: `form.role` ("Organization role"/"Peran organisasi"),
  `form.roleHint`.

**Edit page (same day, follow-up).** `/hr/employees/$employeeId/edit` now has an
organization role card too. It is a *membership* fact, not an employee column,
so it saves through the existing `PATCH /organizations/:id/members/:memberId`
(the endpoint the organization member page uses) instead of the employee PATCH:
`PATCH /human-resources/employees/:id` still does not accept `organizationRoles`.
- `components/hr/employee-edit-form.tsx`: member row resolved from
  `GET /organizations/:id/members` (limit 100 — the contract caps it at 100)
  by `employee.userId`; checkbox grid over `useAssignableOrgRoles` (existing
  grants stay visible, the ladder hides what the caller may not grant);
  separate "Save role" button with its own mutation and member-query
  invalidation.
- First attempt gated the whole card on `member.update`, which hid it for the
  org `hr` role (grants `member: ['read']` only) — reported by the owner as
  "still missing". The card now always renders and only the write controls
  (checkbox enabled state + Save role) are gated; a caller without the grant
  sees the roles read-only (`form.roleReadOnly`). Verified against the dev DB:
  employee `01a20adf-…` has a membership row with `role = 'hr'`, so the lookup
  itself was fine.
- A pending invite has no membership row yet, so the card shows a hint instead
  (`form.roleNoMember`): the role is granted on claim, and no endpoint updates
  a pending invitation's roles.
- Locales en/id: `form.roleNoMember`, `form.roleReadOnly`, `form.rolesLocked`,
  `form.rolesMultiple`, `form.saveRole`; `form.roleHint` shortened to the
  generic wording (it now serves both dialogs).
- Owner follow-up: the checkbox grid was replaced by a single `Select`, the
  same shape `/admin/users` (invite dialog) uses. Saving sends
  `[effectiveRole]`, so it replaces a member's whole comma-joined role set —
  `form.rolesMultiple` warns when the member currently holds more than one.
- Owner follow-up 2: the separate role card is gone; the role field now sits
  inside the "Kepegawaian" (employment) card, below work type and the dates.
- Owner follow-up 3 (browser pass): the role field was a `sm:col-span-2` block
  under a five-field grid, which left the third row half empty and made the
  save button stretch inside the grid. It is now a normal sixth grid cell
  (status/type, work type/hire date, termination date/role), with the hint and
  an outline "Save role" on their own full-width row. Verified in the browser
  on `/hr/employees/01a20adf-…/edit` as an org admin: dropdown lists the
  assignable roles, saving rewrote `auth.members.role` (`hr` → `member`, read
  back from Postgres, then restored to `hr`), no console errors.
- Owner follow-up 4: every `SelectTrigger` in the employment card is `w-full`
  (they were intrinsic-width, narrower than the date pickers), and the grid is
  reordered to status/type, work type/role, hire date/termination date so the
  two dates sit on one row. Re-checked in the browser: six equal columns, no
  console errors.
- Ceiling: the member lookup reads one page of 100 (40 members in the dev
  tenant); an organization with more members would need a `userId` filter on
  the members list.

**Checks.**
- `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` (web-admin): clean.
- `bun test` (web-admin): 209 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test` (packages/locales): 106 pass, 0 fail (en/id parity + dead keys).
- `bunx biome check` on the touched files: clean.
- `bun run lint` (root): 0 errors (18 pre-existing web-admin warnings).
- No browser walk-through.

**Docs.** `backlog.md` ERP-0117 evidence appended. `docs/database/` reviewed:
no table/column/index/constraint change, `docs.dbml` unchanged.

  constraint, logical reference or status vocabulary moved — only the packaging

  database (the last such proof is the 2026-11-21 run; the DDL it proved is

## 2026-11-24 - CI fix for PR #153: payslip tests depended on the local .env

**Failed check:** "Unit Test Backend" (and the JUnit report) on PR #153: three
`hr-payslip.service.test.ts` cases expected `attached` and got `skipped`.
`PayslipService.render` (and `AgreementPdfService.render`) skipped when
`appConfig.pdf.renderBaseUrl` was empty, on top of `renderer.configured`. CI
has no `PDF_RENDER_BASE_URL`/`APP_WEB_URL`; a developer `.env` sets
`APP_WEB_URL`, so it passed locally (Bun loads `.env` even with the variables
emptied in the shell, which is why it did not reproduce at first).

**Fix:** both services gate on `renderer.configured` only -
`ChromiumPdfRenderer.configured` already requires the render base URL in
production, so behaviour there is unchanged. The payslip test now sets
`appConfig.pdf.renderBaseUrl = null` for its run (restored afterwards), so it
behaves like CI everywhere. Checked both ways: under that setting the old
service code fails the same 3 cases CI reported, the fixed code passes 6/6.
Backend `bun test` 1444 pass, backend lint 0 errors, `tsc` clean.

## 2026-11-23 - ERP-0122: payslip PDF on payroll approval (slice 6)

**Scope** (grill-me Q32-Q37, recorded in the ERP-0117 entry below).

**Design gate.** No table, column, index or status change: payslips are
`document.documents` rows (`document_type = payslip`, `status = issued`,
`module = human_resource`, `source_type = employee_salary_record`,
`source_id = employee_salary_records.id`) with their PDF in `document.files`;
`docs/database/` reviewed and unchanged apart from `module-ownership.md`
(the new facade and document contract methods). `validate-dbml` `OK`.
Cross-module reads: `ExportedFinanceService` (new, repository-only, the
facade deferred from ERP-0119), `ExportedUserService.summary` (approver name),
`CompanyService.get`, `DocumentService`, `ExportedNotificationService`.

**Backend.**
- `SalaryService.approve` queues one `payslip-pdf` job per record that
  approval locked (`approvePeriod` now returns the ids); the queue never
  fails the approval.
- `PayslipService.render` (worker): registers the `issued` payslip
  (`DocumentService.issueForSource`), renders `/print/payslips/:id?token=`
  in Chromium, attaches the PDF, notifies the employee in-app
  (`hr.payslip_ready`, `sourceId` = the payslip, so a rerun never doubles it).
  Idempotent (`exists` when the PDF is there); `skipped` without Chromium.
- Public print data at `/human-resources/public/v1/render/payslips/:id?token=`:
  pay lines, net pay, payee account masked to the last four digits, approver
  and date, letterhead.
- `GET /human-resources/salary-records/:id/payslip` and
  `GET /human-resources/salary-records/payslips.zip?period=` (`payroll:read`,
  ERP-0034 scope), `POST /human-resources/salary-records/:id/payslip/regenerate`
  (`payroll:update`, approved records only).
- Self-service `GET /users/me/payslips`, `GET /users/me/payslips/:id/download`
  (session guard; the employee comes from the session user, anyone else's
  record answers 404). The existing `self_service:read_payslip` statement is
  not used: ownership, not a role grant, decides here.
- `DocumentService.issueForSource` and `readFile` (download trail row), optional
  `IObjectStorage.get` (S3 implementation), `ExportedFinanceService`.
- Dependency: `jszip@3.10.2` added to `apps/backend` (already in `bun.lock` as a
  transitive dependency of exceljs; `bun add` downloaded nothing new).

**Web-admin.** Payroll page: "Unduh semua slip gaji (ZIP)" on an approved
period, per-row "Slip gaji" download and "Generate ulang PDF"; print view
`/print/payslips/$documentId` (`payslip-document.tsx`, Indonesian on purpose,
"dibuat secara elektronik", no wet signature); "Slip gaji saya" card on
`/accounts` (`?section=payslips`, the notification deep link), hidden for
non-employees. en/id keys (`hr`, `account`, `notifications`, `api`).

**Commands and outcomes.**

- `bun run test` (root) - 7/7: backend **1440 pass** (new
  `hr-payslip.service.test.ts` 6, the approve-queues-payslips assertion),
  web-admin 209, locales 106, customer-portal 68, landing 25, react-email 6;
  0 fail.
- `bun run lint` - 0 errors; web-admin `tsc` clean, `vite build` built;

`updated_at` not null, partial unique `employee_addresses_primary_uq` (one live
primary), ref to `employees` `delete: restrict`. Migration

creates the month's draft payroll on payday and notifies in-app whoever holds
`payroll:approve`; approval stays manual; overtime pay stays 0.

  `SalaryService.generate` with the company scope (`all`) and no actor

  `records` - not `count`, which i18next reserves for plurals): code list,
  seeder row, en/id `notifications` keys, web `notification-text.ts`.

`appAdminOnly` nav item; the page also refuses non-admins): switch on/off, day
1-31, next run date, explanation of the 01:00 WIB check. en/id keys.

## 2026-11-23 - ERP-0118: HR work schedule (slice 2)

**Scope** (grill-me Q9/Q10, recorded in the ERP-0117 entry below): a weekly

a taken cell, and the new `schedule` permission resource granted like
`attendance`. Attendance is not compared against the schedule yet.

**Design gate.** `docs/database/docs.dbml` (Human Resource `schedules`,

`integrity-and-consistency.md` (soft delete, partial unique) read first. No

`auth.users.id`. Manual grill items: ownership (human_resource), tenant scoping
(through the employee: the ERP-0034 scope, no own `organization_id`), soft

date, `varchar(5)` HH:MM Jakarta, unix-ms timestamps), status vocabulary (none;
`is_day_off` + a CHECK tying the times to it).

**docs.dbml (edited before Drizzle).** `human_resource.schedules`: no longer

before the start is an overnight shift), the intra-module ref to `employees`
is `delete: restrict` (was `cascade`; employees are only soft-deleted).
`gen-logical-references.ts` regenerated (188 refs), `validate-dbml.ts` `OK`.

`20261123121018_erp0118_create_schedules` (SQL inspected: one `CREATE TABLE`,
the partial unique index, the date index, the restrict FK - nothing else).
Its snapshot has two parents and so also merges the two migration branches
`main` carried (`20261123010354_customer_account_owner` and the supplier
drop); `drizzle-kit check` now prints "Everything's fine" (it warned about 3
unmerged branches before) and a second `generate` reports no changes.

`GET /human-resources/schedules/week?start=` (`schedule:read`),
`POST /human-resources/schedules` (`schedule:create`, 409 on a taken day),
`PUT|DELETE /human-resources/schedules/:id` (`schedule:update` / `:delete`),
`POST /human-resources/schedules/fill` (`schedule:create`, at most 62 days,
422 beyond; returns `{created, skipped}`). Date helpers `addDays` /
`weekdayIndex` in `utils/hr.ts`. `packages/common`: `schedule:
['read','create','update','delete']` - owner (spread), `admin` and `hr` all
four, `auditor` read. Seeder `hr-schedules.seeder.ts`: this and next week for

(order Employee, Tasks, Schedule, Attendance, Leave, Overtime, Payroll);

**Owner request** (grill-me, Q1-Q18, all settled in session): implement

feature.

`expense_claim_items`); settlements/advances untouched. (2) Approval is the
ledger event (accrual), not cash. (3) Paying a claim (`paid`, `payment_id`) is

`chart_of_accounts.code`; no COA seeder added. (6) Dialog line editor + table.

`draft`; `cancelled` only from `draft`/`submitted`; an approved claim is
corrected through the existing journal reversal. (10) Receipts deferred. (11)
VAT per line, total derived server-side. (12) Two tables per DBML. (13) DBML
CHECK kept verbatim; unit tests. (14) Server filters + whitelisted sort. (15)
Detail page `$claimId`. (16) `accountant: read|approve|reject`. (17) Detail
carries lines, workflow actions and the posted entry. (18) Editing lives on the
detail page only.

column set, so no table was invented; the only DBML edits are dropping
`status: target` from both notes and marking `updated_at` `[not null]` to match

## 2026-11-23 - ERP-0114: `/crm/customers` robustness, one account per customer, one owner per company, global form conventions

**Owner request** (grill-me, Q1-Q34, all settled in session): make
`/crm/customers` robust - forms aligned to `customer.*` and grouped by use,
"(Optional)" on optional fields, the E.164 `CountryPhoneField`, "Rp" money
fields, no number spinner (globally in web-admin); a TanStack table with
dropdown filters, pagination, sort, the customer photo and company; a Better
Auth account created with every customer (username from the name + 6 digits
of the timestamp, password `{username}12345678`).

**Design gate (Gate 1 + 2).** Read `docs.dbml` (customer, identity modules),
`module-ownership.md`, `integrity-and-consistency.md`; manual grilling pass
(the `grilling` skill was available this time). Decisions:
- Ownership: all tables stay in schema `customer`; the account stays in
  `auth` behind `ExportedUserService` (no cross-schema FK, no `auth` query from
  the customer module). Company-wide (no `organization_id`, ADR-0011).
- **One Better Auth account = one `customer.customers` row** (Q34): created
  with the person, kept on revoke, email lives on the account (Q5:
  `customers.email` dropped), required on create; verified at the first portal
  sign-in and locked afterwards (Q14/Q23); username always
  `{base}_{last 6 ms digits}` (Q19/Q27); default password; credentials shown
  once to staff **and** emailed (Q17/Q26); `portal_password_change_required`
  set (Q7b; enforcement is ERP-0115, Q32).
- **One owner per customer company + N staff** (Q29c): new
  `companies.owner_customer_id` (intra-schema FK `on delete set null`, unique
  among live rows); `customers.is_primary`, `customers.owner_user_id`,
  `companies.owner_user_id` dropped (Q25/Q30); the portal role is derived
  from the column (`utils/ownership.ts`).
- `whatsapp` dropped from both tables (Q9/Q12): the phone (E.164) is the
  WhatsApp number; frozen document snapshots keep their `whatsapp` key.
- Photo = `auth.users.image` via the user module, uploaded from the form
  (Q2/Q22/Q28). Sort on the server (Q3). Inline "new company" from the person
  form, the person becomes its owner (Q24). Customer companies are data
  records only (Q15).
- Money/datetime: no money column touched; timestamps unchanged (unix ms).
  Soft delete: unchanged; an inline company is soft-deleted on a failed create.

**Schema** (`docs.dbml` first, then Drizzle, then the generators):
- `customer.customers`: - `email`, `whatsapp`, `is_primary`, `owner_user_id`
  (+ their indexes); + `portal_password_change_required boolean not null default false`.
- `customer.companies`: - `whatsapp`, `owner_user_id`; + `owner_customer_id uuid`
  (FK, partial unique index `customer_companies_owner_uq`).
- Migration `database/migrations/20261123010354_customer_account_owner`
  (generated with `--hints` for the three new objects; SQL inspected: 3 index
  drops, 2 adds, 6 column drops, 1 unique index, 1 FK). No backfill: nothing
  is deployed (ADR-0024 Q34). No customer seeder exists, so seeds are
  unaffected.

**Backend.** `customer`: new `CustomerAccountService` (username, default
password, provisioning with compensation, credentials mail), `CustomerService`
create/update with account, inline company, ownership transfer, email lock,
`POST|DELETE /customers/people/:id/photo` (`customer:update`), list sort
(`sort`, `order`) and email search through `ExportedUserService.findIdsByEmail`;
list/detail rows carry `account`, `company`, `isOwner` (people) and `owner`
(companies). `PortalAccountService`: invites of new contacts use the create
path (credentials email), revoke keeps `user_id`, role derived from the
owner column, invite with role owner moves ownership, the owner cannot close
their login, first sign-in verifies the email, password change clears the
flag. `ExportedCustomerService`: email from the account, no `whatsapp`.
`user`: `ExportedUserService` + account gateway (`createCustomerAccount`,

## 2026-11-23 - ERP-0112: last used login method badge on /login

User request: apply Better Auth's `lastLoginMethod` in the web admin.
Decisions (plan-mode round): **cookie only** (`storeInDatabase` off — no
`auth.users` column, no migration, `docs/database/` unchanged); production
cookie scope is an open decision (dev ports and one origin work; separate
subdomains need `advanced.crossSubDomainCookies`), recorded below.

**Backend.** `plugins/last-login-method.auth.ts`:
`lastLoginMethod({ customResolveMethod })` with the pure
`resolveLoginMethodOverride` mapping `/sign-in/username` to `username`
(the library default does not know that endpoint, and the login form uses it
for non-email identifiers); every other path returns `null` so Better Auth's
own mapping applies (`email`, the OAuth callback's provider id, `passkey`,
`magic-link`, `email-otp`). Registered in `plugin.auth.ts`. Cookie:
`better-auth.last_used_login_method`, `httpOnly: false`, 30 days, written
only when a session cookie is set.

**Web-admin.** `lib/auth-client.ts` adds `lastLoginMethodClient()`;
`lib/last-login.ts` validates the client-writable cookie against
`LAST_LOGIN_METHODS` (`parseLastLoginMethod`, `readLastLoginMethod`,
`clearLastLoginMethodIf`); `login-form.tsx` badges "Last used" next to the
Login button (`email`/`username`) or on the Google button, which is also
promoted to the default variant when it was the last method;
`connected-accounts-card.tsx` clears the cookie when Google is disconnected so
the badge never points at a removed method. Locale key
`auth:login.lastUsed` in en + id.

**Tests.** Backend `test/unit/last-login-method.auth.test.ts` (2),
web-admin `test/unit/last-login.test.ts` (2, incl. unknown/injected values).

## 2026-11-21 - ERP-0111: account settings on one page, profile editor, email verification, Google linking

User request: improve `/profiles`, `/profiles/edit` and `/account`. Decisions
taken in the plan-mode session: one `/accounts` page of cards instead of the
`/account`, `/account/email`, `/account/sessions` tabs; `/profiles` opens the
editor directly (detail view removed); username moves to account settings;
the photo uses the `/organizations/new` dropzone and uploads on Save; bio is a
textarea; Google can be linked only with the same email (Better Auth default);
change-email mails the new address only (no old-address confirmation);
verification is not required to sign in; spacing tightened at page level,
`packages/ui` defaults untouched. No redirects from the removed routes
(nothing deployed).

**Gates.** No table, column or cross-module reference changes, so
`docs/database/` was reviewed and is unchanged (only `auth.users` /
`auth.accounts` rows owned by Better Auth are read and written through its
API). The design was settled in the plan-mode question rounds instead of the
`grill-me` skill; the answers above are the record.

**Backend (`providers/better-auth`, options only).**
- `options/change-email.auth.ts`: `user.changeEmail.enabled: true`. Before
  this, Better Auth answered every `/change-email` with
  `CHANGE_EMAIL_DISABLED`, so the web email form had never worked.
- `options/email-verification-policy.auth.ts`: `expiresIn: 3600`,
  `autoSignInAfterVerification: false`, spread into the verification options.
- `options/user-cache.auth.ts` + `databaseHooks.user.update.after`: evicts
  `user:id:<id>` and `user:all`. Better Auth writes `auth.users` itself
  (update-user, admin API, verify-email, change-email), bypassing
  `UserRepository`'s cache, so `GET /users/me` served the old bio / username
  / email / verification state for up to `USER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` (300 s).
  Found during the browser check: a saved bio was not shown back.
- Test: `test/unit/email-change-verification.auth.test.ts` (7, no module
  mocks: Bun's `mock.module` would leak into `mailer.test.ts`).

**Frontend (web-admin).**
- Routes: `_authed.accounts.tsx` (validated search
  `section/verified/linked/error`, reads the Better Auth return once, clears
  it with `resetScroll: false`, scrolls to the card) and `_authed.profiles.tsx`;
  removed `_authed.account*.tsx`, `_authed.profiles.{index,edit}.tsx`,
  `profile-view.tsx`, unused `profile/sessions-table.tsx`.
  `routeTree.gen.ts` regenerated by `vite build`. Nav user menu -> `/accounts`.
- Cards: `username-card.tsx` (live `/username-availability`, derived state),
  `email-card.tsx` (status badge, send verification with 60 s cooldown, link
  outcome alert, change-email with pending note and same-address guard),
  `connected-accounts-card.tsx` (`listAccounts` / `linkSocial` /
  `unlinkAccount` by account row id; last sign-in method cannot be
  unlinked), `password-card.tsx` (change form, or a password-setup link via
  `requestPasswordReset` for provider-only users — Better Auth's reset creates
  the missing credential account), `sessions-table.tsx` (compact, bulk revoke
  in the header, truncated user agent).
- `profile-edit-form.tsx`: dropzone photo, name, bio textarea with counter

- Shared: `components/image-dropzone.tsx` (moved from `organization/`),

  `lib/account-search.ts` (callback URLs, outcome parsing; absolute and

### Follow-up: `/login` hardening, invitation-only Google sign-in (ADR-0029)

User request: a Google sign-in for someone who was not invited must not get
in. Findings before the change: an unknown Google email **created** an
`auth.users` row (Better Auth social sign-up default); a pending invitee
(pre-created with `emailVerified: true`) was implicitly linked and, if
invited as application admin, passed the role-only gate without claiming;
no sign-in path read `status`/`deletedAt`, so a deactivated user could sign
in again; the web Google callback was relative (landed on the API origin)
and gate refusals showed as raw JSON there.

- Backend: `options/social-providers.auth.ts` `buildSocialProviders` with
  `disableSignUp: true`; `ac/login-gate.ts` `isAccountActive` +
  `webAdminDenial` (codes `ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE`, `WEB_ADMIN_ACCESS_DENIED`);
  `session.auth.ts` gate reads `status`/`deletedAt`, throws coded errors
  translated from the request language (`api` keys `auth.accountNotActive`,
  `auth.webAdminAccessDenied`); `options/account-link.auth.ts`
  `databaseHooks.account.create.before` refuses a social account for an
  inactive or missing owner (`credential` exempt for the claim).
- Web: `lib/login-error.ts` (`loginErrorKey`, `sameOriginUrl`,
  `loginErrorCallbackUrl`); `login-form.tsx` sends absolute same-origin
  `callbackURL` + `errorCallbackURL`; `/login` validates `error`, shows the
  mapped `auth` message once and clears it (`redirect` kept).
- Docs: ADR-0029 (amends the ADR-0017/0018 login gate),
  `security-and-access.md` "Sign-in" section and cache note.

## 2026-11-23 - ERP-0110: components and materials of a product (composition / BOM)

**Owner request** (via grill-me, all 13 questions answered "yes"): on the product
CRUD, show the components or materials a product is made of.

**Decisions.** Informational only (no stock movement, no costing, not in the
public catalog or quotation PDFs). New `product.product_components`
(`product_id` cascade, `component_id` restrict, `quantity numeric(18,3) > 0`,
`sort_order`, soft delete, partial unique per live pair, `product_id <>
component_id`); no `organization_id` (tenant comes from the parent). Parent must
be `product_kind = 'product'`; lines must be live `component`/`material`,
visible to the parent's organization (global parent -> global items only);
max 50 lines, no duplicates. Archiving a used component is allowed; its line
shows "Archived" and must be dropped on the next save.

**Backend.** `GET|PUT /products/:id/components` (`product:read` / `product:update`;
PUT replaces the whole list in one transaction), `GET /products/:id` also returns
`components`. `ProductComponentRepository` / `ProductComponentService`, errors
`product.compositionParentKind` and `product.componentNotUsable` (en + id).
Migration `20261122200931_add_product_components`; `docs.dbml` edited first.
Seeder: `CTRL-DOOR-01` gets 1x `CMP-PSU-12V` + 3 m `MAT-CABLE-CAT6`.

**Web-admin.** Detail page: "Components & materials" table (links to each item,
archived badge). Create dialog and edit page: `ProductCompositionEditor`
(server-side search over components + materials, quantity per row), saved with
`PUT` after the product; a failed save toasts and keeps the product. Locale keys
`product:composition.*` (en + id).

`validate-dbml.ts` OK (152 intra-module refs, 0 drift); backend `bunx tsc` clean,

authorization doubles extended); web-admin `tsc` clean, `bun test` 174 pass;
locales `bun test` 106 pass; `bun run lint` 0 errors. Product seeder run twice via
`seedProduct()`: 2 live lines after run 1, still 2 after run 2 (the full
`drizzle:seed` stops earlier on an already-existing admin username, unrelated).
New routes answer 401 without a session on a fresh backend instance.

session untested end to end. `docs/database/` updated (table, refs, regenerated

## 2026-11-22 - ERP-0107: Docker Hub images + CI for web-landing and web-customer-portal (Bun only)

**Owner request.** Dockerfile and GitHub workflow for both Astro apps, published
to Docker Hub as `ims-erp-landing` and `ims-erp-customer-portal`, added to the
root compose; follow-up the same day: "Gunakan bun" (no Node anywhere) and a
new branch from `main` (`ci/erp-0107-astro-docker-images`).

**Found.** Both Dockerfiles and compose services already existed (`4fbe20f0`)
under the image names `ims-erp-web-landing` / `ims-erp-web-customer-portal`,
ran the server on `node:22-alpine`, and had no workflow. The portal image did
**not** build: `astro build` ran on Bun and two PWA dependencies,
`@vite-pwa/workbox-build@8.0.15` and `@unplugin-pwa/core@0.0.7`, statically
import `findPackageJSON` from `node:module`, which Bun 1.4.5 does not have
(`Export named 'findPackageJSON' not found in module 'node:module'`). Bun also
rewrites `ns.findPackageJSON` on a namespace import back into a named import,
so only a runtime lookup avoids the link error.

**Changed.**
- `patches/` + root `patchedDependencies` (via `bun patch` / `bun patch --commit`):
  both files look the function up with
  `process.getBuiltinModule("node:module").findPackageJSON`; when it is missing
  (Bun) `workbox-build` walks up `node_modules`, `unplugin-pwa` uses its
  existing `createRequire` fallback. Node behaviour is unchanged.
- `apps/web-{landing,customer-portal}/Dockerfile`: every stage on
  `oven/bun:1.4-alpine`; copy `patches/` before `bun install`; build with
  `bun --bun run`; runtime `CMD ["bun", "/app/dist/server/entry.mjs"]` as the
  image's `bun` user; telemetry off.
- `apps/{backend,web-admin}/Dockerfile`: copy `patches/` too (a frozen install
  needs the patch files once `patchedDependencies` exists).
- New workflows `main-test-and-build-web-{landing,customer-portal}.yml`
  (paths filter, `bun --bun run … typecheck`, `bun test`, Docker build without
  push) and `main-deploy-web-{landing,customer-portal}.yml` (merged PR to
  `main` → push `okifirsyah404/ims-erp-landing` /
  `okifirsyah404/ims-erp-customer-portal`, tags `sha-<sha>` + `dev`, `PUBLIC_*`
  build args from repository variables), modelled on the web-admin pair.
- `docker-compose.yml` / `docker-compose.local.yml`: image names switched to
  the new repositories. Runbook and `stack-compatibility.md` updated.

**Checks (local, Docker 27.2.0, Bun 1.4.4 host / 1.4.5 image).**
- `docker build -f apps/<app>/Dockerfile .` for web-landing,
  web-customer-portal, web-admin and backend → all exit 0.
- Containers: PID 1 is `bun /app/dist/server/entry.mjs`, user `bun`, no log
  errors. Landing (`WEB_DATA_SOURCE=demo`) `/` 200, `/products` 200; portal
  (`PORTAL_DATA_SOURCE=demo`) `/` 303, `/login` 200, `/sw.js` 200,
  `/manifest.webmanifest` 200; `/app/.astro/session` writable.
- `bun --bun run build` in the portal → Complete (also with Node: Complete).
- `bun run --cwd packages/common build`, then `bun --bun run --cwd apps/<app> typecheck`
  → 0 errors for both (one earlier exit 9 without output happened while four
  Docker builds ran in parallel; re-run clean); `bun test` landing 25 pass,
  portal 68 pass.
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile` → no changes;
  `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml config --images`
  lists `ims-erp-landing:local` / `ims-erp-customer-portal:local`;
  `bunx yaml-lint` on the four workflows → successful.

**Not done.** Workflows not run on GitHub Actions; the Docker Hub
repositories and the `main-deploy` environment secrets
(`DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` / `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`) must exist before the first push.
Root `bun run test` / `lint` not re-run (no TS source changed).
`docs/database/` reviewed and unchanged (no schema change).

decision, once PR #139 is reviewed.

## 2026-11-22 - Item list filters like the warehouse list, plus price and stock sliders

- No backlog item; `docs/database/` unchanged (no schema change). `GET /products` gains `status` (`all|active|inactive`), `minPrice`/`maxPrice`
  (selling price, IDR minor units), `minStock`/`maxStock` (available quantity summed over every bin; no stock row counts as 0) and
  `sortBy` (`name|code|price`) / `sortDir`. New `GET /products/ranges?productKind=` returns `{ maxSellingPrice, maxStock }` for the slider
  bounds (`product:read`, static route before `/:id`).
- Stock is an `inventory` fact (ADR-0026): `IStockRepository.availableTotals()` -> `ExportedInventoryService.availableTotals()`; the product
  repository turns it into an id predicate with the pure `stockRangePredicate` (`NOT IN` rows outside the range when the range includes 0, so
  products without a stock row still match; `IN` otherwise). 5 unit tests for it; test doubles got `ranges`/`availableTotals`.
- Web: `ItemFiltersPopover` (Funnel button with an active-count, Reset/Apply, drafts re-seeded on open) on the three list pages with category,
  status, price (`Slider` + two `MoneyInput`), stock (`Slider` + two numeric `Input`) and sort. A thumb parked on a bound means "no limit", so
  the URL only holds what narrows the list; prices live in rupiah in the URL and the list converts to minor units. The old inline category
  select and "active only" checkbox are gone (`?activeOnly=true` links still read as `status=active`). Pure helpers in
  `lib/item-filter-draft.ts` and `lib/item-list-search.ts` (tested).
- Verified: backend `bun test` 1334 pass, `tsc` clean; live API probe against the running backend (ranges, price/status/sort/stock params all
  200 with the expected rows); web-admin `tsc` clean, `bun test` 172 pass; locales 106 pass. **Not verified:** the popover in a browser, and the

## 2026-11-21 - Product / Component / Material CRUD fixes, Rupiah `MoneyInput`, Products as its own nav item

- No `ERP-*` item claimed (follow-up to ERP-0043/0063/0076); `docs/database/` reviewed and unchanged (no schema change).
- **Navigation bugs fixed.** (1) `/inventory/items/:id/edit` never rendered: `$itemId.edit.tsx` nested under `$itemId.tsx`, which had no
  `<Outlet/>`, so the detail page showed instead of the form. (2) Breadcrumbs linked to routes that do not exist (`/inventory`,
  `/inventory/items`) and showed English/UUID labels. (3) Archive always returned to `/products`. (4) The "Item categories" menu was
  permanently hidden (no permission) and sat under the `/products` prefix. (5) Detail/edit highlighted no menu.
- **Routes per kind** (decision with the user): `/products/$productId[/edit]`, `/inventory/components/$productId[/edit]`,
  `/inventory/materials/$productId[/edit]` (folder layout, no dot-nesting); `/inventory/items/*` removed (nothing is deployed).
  Shared `ItemDetailPage`/`ItemEditPage` take `kind` and redirect an item opened under the wrong kind; links go through
  `lib/item-routes.ts`. Categories moved to `/product-categories` (matches the API and the menu url) and are gated by `product.read`.
- **Nav:** Products is a top-level item of the Inventory section; the "Items" group (icon `Boxes`) keeps components, materials, stock,
  adjustments, categories, movements. Breadcrumbs: labels for components/materials/stock pages, item name on detail, crumbs for
  grouping prefixes without a route are dropped (`buildCrumbs(..., routeExists)` fed by `router.routesByPath`).
- **Money unit bug:** `ItemForm` sent the typed rupiah as minor units (no x100) and the detail page printed the raw number, while
  quotations read `sellingPrice` as sen (`minorToRupiah`). The form now uses `rupiahToMinor`/`minorToRupiah` and the detail uses
  `formatIdr`. Rows saved earlier hold rupiah-as-sen: reseed or correct (no production database).
- **`MoneyInput`** (`components/money-input.tsx`, `lib/money-input.ts`): `InputGroup` + "Rp" prefix, `type='text'`, `id-ID` grouping,
  canonical value `"1500000.5"` so `rupiahToMinor` is unchanged; tested. Applied to 33 money fields: item prices, adjustment unit cost,
  quotation unit price/discount, PO unit price, PR estimate, lead value, contract value, asset cost/depreciation/proceeds, billing
  amount, project cost, ticket cost, receipt amount, payroll amounts, and the finance/tax inline forms (cash-bank, bills, opening
  balances, journal debit/credit, reconciliation, tax base/amount, withholding, corrections). Quantities, percentages, days and
  years stay numeric. Not migrated: any money field that was not an `Input` bound to the names above - the audit was by search
  (`type='number'`, `toMinor`, `* 100`), not exhaustive reading of every form.
- **List search/filter:** product, component and material lists have search (name/SKU/brand), category and "active only" in the URL
  (`lib/item-list-search.ts`, `validateItemListSearch`); archived items are intentionally not listed (no restore endpoint, and the
  detail endpoint rejects archived rows).
- **Backend:** `ProductService.updateProduct` refuses to flip `isSerialized` while the product has live units (3 new tests).
  Materials are unchanged (user decision: serialized stays allowed).
- Verified: backend `bun test` 1329 pass, `tsc` clean; web-admin `tsc` clean, `bun test` 165 pass; locales 106 pass;
  `validate-dbml.ts` OK. **Not verified in a browser** (no login in this session): the new routes, active menu, breadcrumbs,
  the caret behaviour of `MoneyInput` while editing mid-number, and the redirect between kinds.

scoping, soft delete, money and dates are unaffected.

## 2026-11-21 - ERP-0094 amended: the `customer` role is checked by the customer portal, not the ERP

Owner request on PR #139 (`feat/erp-0094-portal-session-cookie`): the ERP
cannot tell which client sent a request (web admin, customer portal,
website), so the `customer` role check belongs to the portal. ADR-0027
decision 2 amended in place (dated note).

**Changed.**
- Backend `customer`: `PortalAuthService` no longer refuses a session without
  the `customer` role (`login`, `verifyLoginCode`, `verifySignup`, `resolve`);
  it still requires a live session and an active portal login. The roles
  travel on `PortalContext.roles` (`src/authorization/portal-auth.ts`) and are
  returned as `user.roles` by `portalUser()` (sign-in bodies, `/me`).
  `PORTAL_CUSTOMER_ROLE` removed from `portal.contract.ts`. The identity
  module still grants the role with every portal login (unchanged).
- `apps/web-customer-portal`: `PortalUser.roles` + zod schema;
  `src/lib/portal-role.ts` (`isPortalCustomer`); the `login`,
  `verifyLoginCode` and `verifyEmail` actions end the fresh ERP session and
  answer like a wrong password for a login without `customer`; the middleware
  drops a stored session whose user lacks the role (sessions stored before
  this change have no `roles` and are signed out once).
- Tests: `portal-account.test.ts` - the two "no `customer` role → 401" cases
  now assert the roles are passed through; new
  `apps/web-customer-portal/src/lib/portal-role.test.ts`; `erp-source.test.ts`
  fixture carries `roles`.
- Docs: ADR-0027, `docs/architecture/modules/customer-portal.md`,
  `backlog.md` ERP-0094, `features.md`. `docs/database/` reviewed and
  unchanged (no table, column or vocabulary change).

**Commands.**
- `cd packages/common && bun run build` - needed first: the local `dist` was
  stale (7 typecheck errors and 6 test load errors on `employmentTypeSchema` /
  `assignableOrganizationRoles`, present without this change too).
- `cd apps/backend && bun test` → 1333 pass / 0 fail; `bunx tsc --noEmit` → 0
  errors; `bun run lint` → exit 0, no warning in touched files.
- `cd apps/web-customer-portal && bun test` → 66 pass / 0 fail;
  `bun run typecheck` (`astro check`) → 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `bun docs/database/validate-dbml.ts` → OK.

**Not done.** Not re-checked live; the earlier live check "login without
`customer` → 401" now answers 200 at the ERP and is refused by the portal.
No browser walk-through. Not reviewed.

## 2026-11-21 - ERP-0106: portal security settings - two-step sign-in, active devices, delete own login (port of branch ERP-0081)

Port step P1 (second half) of `docs/plan/port-portal-onto-main.md`, decision

**Gates.** Gate 1: read `docs/database/docs.dbml` (`// MODULE:` index, Customer
block: `customer.companies`, `customer.customers` portal columns and checks),
`module-ownership.md` (Customer owns the people incl. the portal login;
Identity: profile/preferences are no longer separate tables) and
`data-dictionary.md` 1.11 (boolean flags) and 6 (checks). The booleans keep
the names port plan D3 fixed (`portal_two_step`, `portal_push`, grouped with
the other `portal_*` login columns) instead of the `is_*` pattern; the closed
`portal_language` vocabulary gets a check as section 6 asks. Skipped
`integrity-and-consistency.md` (no FK, uniqueness or concurrency rule
changes), `logical-references.md` (no new cross-module id column) and
`implementation-phases.md` (nothing depends on an unlanded step). Gate 2: the design was settled by port plan D3 (columns on
`customer.customers`, not `auth.user_preferences`) and the branch's owner
decisions of 2026-11-20 (2-step opt-in, delete login keeps data, only owner
refused); answers recorded: module ownership - settings, 2-step, devices and
delete login stay in `customer` (sessions through the customer's own Better

money; status vocabulary unchanged. "Only owner" on main = an `owner` login
with a `company_id` and no other `active` owner among the company's live
logins; an individual customer (no company) is their own account and may
delete their login.

## 2026-11-23 - ADR-0026: product and warehouse become their own modules (schema split)

User request: separate `product` and `warehouse` from the inventory database
schema and give each its own module; then move both onto their own API
prefixes, move the whole frontend slice out of `inventory`, and give each
module its own numbering series (`{COMPANY}` added to the pattern) and its own
`settings` table. Decision record: `docs/architecture/decisions/ADR-0026-product-and-warehouse-modules.md`
(supersedes the single-schema part of ADR-0008 and ADR-0024 Q14).

**Schema (T1).** 20 Postgres schemas, 192 tables (188 before).
`drizzle/schemas/product.schema.ts` owns `products`, `product_categories`,
`settings`, `code_numberings`; `drizzle/schemas/warehouse.schema.ts` owns the
six estate tables plus `settings` and `code_numberings`. `inventory` keeps 20
tables. 16 former FKs from `inventory` into the moved tables became plain
nullable uuid columns with the standard logical-reference note (ADR-0014):
`item_serials.{product_id,warehouse_id,bin_id}`, `items.{warehouse_id,storage_id}`,
`documents.product_id`, `movements.{product_id,warehouse_id,bin_id,target_warehouse_id,target_bin_id}`,
`stocks.{product_id,warehouse_id,bin_id}`, `stock_adjustments.warehouse_id`,
`stock_adjustment_items.{product_id,bin_id}`.

**Cross-module reads (T3).** Every join/EXISTS across the new boundary is
gone: stock valuation (products + warehouses + storages joins) now batches
through the two facades and a `searchByNameOrSku` id set; `movement.repository`
takes `warehouseIds` from `idsInScope`; `product.repository` asks
`productIdsInWarehouse`/`availableByProducts`/`countSerials`;
`warehouse.repository` lost `countKinds`/`countLiveUnits` (now
`countSerialKindsByWarehouse`, `countMaterialStocks`, `countItemsByWarehouse`,
`countLiveUnits` on the inventory facade + a local `countStorages`).

**Cycle breaker.** `ExportedInventoryService ↔ ExportedProductService` is a
real object-graph cycle. A factory registration for the port was not enough
(tsyringe follows the lambda's emitted `design:paramtypes`), so the product
kind lookup is now `ProductKindsPort`, constructed with a lazily-resolving
closure (`useFactory: (c) => new ProductKindsPort(() => c.resolve(...))`) and
the serial count flows the other way through `PRODUCT_SERIAL_COUNTS_TOKEN`.
Boot verified: `scripts/__boot-check.ts` (throwaway) resolved both facades
against the seeded disposable DB and returned a product snapshot, the
warehouse name map and the serial-kind counts.

**Movement (T5) - regenerated baseline.** `drizzle-kit generate` after the
split produced one migration: 20 `CREATE SCHEMA`, 168 `CREATE TABLE`, only
intra-module FKs. The previous baseline was archived to
`database/migrations-archive/v2-product-warehouse-20261123` (same convention
as `v1`) and the new one is `database/migrations/20261120192010_parched_venom`
(`migration.sql` + `snapshot.json`, no `meta/` - matches the repo's baseline
layout). A second `generate` reports "No schema changes". Applied to a
disposable database `ims_erp_split_check`: `migrate` OK, `seed` OK
(products 3, categories 11, warehouses 2, storages 3, serials 2, items 6), a
second `seed` inserted 0 rows (idempotent).

`bunx --bun drizzle-kit generate` → one migration, then "No schema changes, nothing to migrate".
`POSTGRES_URL=…/ims_erp_split_check bunx --bun drizzle-kit migrate` → applied.
`POSTGRES_URL=…/ims_erp_split_check bun run drizzle:seed` twice → second run 0 new rows.
`bun docs/database/gen-logical-references.ts` → 190 refs, 25 targets, 147 intra-module refs.
`bun docs/database/validate-dbml.ts` → `parsed: 192 tables, 147 refs / cross-module refs: 0 / timestamp gaps: 0 / drizzle parity drift: 0 / column parity drift: 0 / OK`.
`cd packages/locales && bun test` → 98 pass, 0 fail (locale parity + dead keys).

**Docs.** `docs/database/docs.dbml` (new `MODULE: Product` / `MODULE: Warehouse`

## 2026-11-22 - Backend: every paginated repository method is `paginate()` on one shared envelope helper

User request: make `apps/backend/src/app/*` use `paginate()` instead of `list()`
and friends, following the `location` module as the reference. No `ERP-*`
backlog item is claimed (internal refactor: no endpoint, envelope, or schema
change), so `backlog.md` / `features.md` do not move. `docs/database/` reviewed
and unchanged — no table, column, index, constraint, status vocabulary, or
column type changed; the grill-me pass had nothing to grill (tenant scoping and
soft-delete filters are unchanged, only their argument plumbing moved).

New shared helper `apps/backend/src/utils/pagination.util.ts`:
`paginationResult(request, total, data)` builds `TPaginationResult<T>` with
`totalPages = Math.ceil(total / limit)`. Every repository now uses it instead of
hand-rolling `meta` — the old code had drifted across three spellings
(`Math.ceil(...)`, `Math.ceil(...) || 1`, `Math.max(1, ...)`), so the same empty
list reported 1 page in some modules and 0 in others.

Renamed + reshaped to `paginate(request)` / `paginate<Thing>(request)` with one
request object (`TPaginationRequest & { ...filters }`, tenant inside):

- `audit` `list` -> `paginate`; `notification` `listForUser` ->
  `paginateForUser`; `payment` `list` -> `paginate`; `user`
  `invitation.list` -> `paginate`, `user-management.listUsers` ->

## 2026-11-21 - Migrations re-split into one folder per Postgres schema

User request: create one migration per schema in
`apps/backend/database/migrations/` named `<datetime>_create_<schema>_schema`,
derived from `apps/backend/drizzle/schemas/`. This restores ADR-0024 decision 6
("per-schema baseline", extending ADR-0019), which the 2026-11-19/20 P8 cutover
had shipped as a single folder.

**What changed.** The single baseline `20261120192010_parched_venom` is archived
to `database/migrations-archive/v3-per-schema-20261121` (same convention as
`v1` and `v2-product-warehouse-20261123`) and replaced by **20 folders**:

`20261120214111_create_auth_schema`, `..._create_audit_schema`,
`..._create_automation_schema`, `..._create_company_schema`,
`..._create_customer_schema`, `..._create_document_schema`,
`..._create_finance_schema`, `..._create_human_resource_schema`,
`..._create_inventory_schema`, `..._create_location_schema`,
`..._create_notification_schema`, `..._create_payment_schema`,
`..._create_procurement_schema`, `..._create_product_schema`,
`..._create_project_schema`, `..._create_sale_schema`,
`..._create_supplier_schema`, `..._create_tax_schema`,
`..._create_ticket_schema`, `..._create_warehouse_schema`.

`auth` is first (Better Auth owns the foundation tables), the rest alphabetical.
The database has **0 cross-schema foreign keys**, so the order is a readability
choice, not a correctness requirement — every folder is self-contained.

**Generated, not hand-assembled.** Each folder came from `drizzle-kit generate`
run against a **cumulative** `--schema` list (`audit.schema.ts`, then
`audit + automation`, …), so the chain is 1 `base` + 19 chained `diff`
snapshots: `check` and `generate` agree with `drizzle/schemas` by construction.
No SQL statement was written or edited by hand.

**Equivalence proven before the swap.** Two independent checks, both run before
the old folder was removed:

- Concatenating the 20 folders yields the **same 728 statements** as the
  archived baseline (same multiset; 0 missing, 0 extra). Statement counts per
  schema also matched the archived `snapshot.json` footprints exactly
  (audit 7, auth 40, automation 17, company 10, customer 25, document 41,
  finance 87, human_resource 43, inventory 106, location 16, notification 11,
  payment 20, procurement 42, product 17, project 78, sale 76, supplier 21,
  tax 21, ticket 18, warehouse 32).
- A fresh `generateMigration(empty → drizzle/schemas)` reproduced the archived
  `migration.sql` with **0 statement-level differences**, confirming the old
  baseline carried no hand-written SQL tail (the ADR-0019 exception for
  `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` / partial index predicates no longer applies — the
  current snapshot models them).

**Commands run (2026-11-21).**
`bunx --bun drizzle-kit generate` (per-schema, cumulative `--schema`) → 20
folders. `bunx --bun drizzle-kit generate` against the repo config → "No schema
changes, nothing to migrate". `bunx --bun drizzle-kit check` → "Everything's
fine". On a disposable `postgres:18-alpine` container
(`POSTGRES_URL=postgresql://ci:ci@localhost:55432/perschema_check`):
`drizzle-kit migrate` → applied; resulting database = 22 schemas, 169 tables
(168 application + the `drizzle` journal table's schema), 20 journal rows,
**0 cross-schema FKs**. `bun run database/seeders/index.ts` → seeded; second run
→ 0 inserts (idempotent). `pg_dump --schema-only` of that database vs. one
migrated from the archived single baseline → **identical** (9669 lines each,
differing only in pg_dump's random `\restrict` session tokens).
`bun docs/database/validate-dbml.ts` → `OK` (192 tables, 147 refs, 0
cross-module refs, 0 timestamp gaps, 0 drizzle parity drift, 0 column parity
drift).

**Docs.** `runbook.md` (baseline section), `data-model.md`, `project-audit.md`,
`architecture/README.md`, `database/implementation-phases.md` (new P8b) and
`AGENTS.md` (command-status row) now describe the per-schema chain; the
single-baseline references are marked superseded, not deleted.
`docs/database/docs.dbml` was reviewed and is **unchanged** — no table, column,
index, constraint, cross-module link or status vocabulary moved; only the
packaging of the same DDL changed.

## 2026-11-21 - Invite dialog: role ladder enforced end to end, permanent/temporary switch, employee email fix

User request (2026-11-21): the user-invitation dialog on `/admin/users` and
`/organizations/<id>` offered every organization role to everyone, and an
invited employee could not be marked temporary. Two further requests during
the session: fix the same bug on the member-edit page, and add the
`employmentType` column to the bulk template.

**Role ladder (requirements 1-3).** One shared helper now owns the rule
(`assignableOrganizationRoles` / `grantableOrganizationRoles` in
`packages/common/src/authorization/erp-permissions.ts`):

| Caller | invited roles |
| --- | --- |
| anyone | never `owner` |
| org `admin` | never `owner`, `admin` |
| org `hr` | never `owner`, `admin`, `hr` |
| platform `admin` (`user.role`) | never `owner` (unless they also hold an owner membership) |

- `components/invite/invite-dialog.tsx`: the dropdown renders
  `grantableRoles` for the **target** organization (in admin mode it follows
  the organization selector), and the effective role is clamped during render
  rather than in an effect, so switching organizations can never leave a
  now-illegal value selected. `lib/use-caller-org-roles.ts` resolves the
  caller's membership from `GET /organizations/mine`.
- `lib/admin-api.ts` (`parseBulkInviteRows`) and
  `packages/common/src/files/invite-sheet.ts` (`rowsToInviteSheet`) accept
  `allowedRoles`; a disallowed role is a per-row error.
- The sheet parser's hand-copied `ERP_ROLES` list is gone — it still named the
  app roles `investor`/`customer` removed by ADR-0018, so a sheet using them
  passed the client and was rejected row-by-row by the API. It now reads
  `erpRoleNames`.
- **Backend enforcement** (`src/authorization/role-assignment.ts`, new):
  `POST /admin/invitations`, `POST /organizations/:id/invitations` (single and
  bulk — the batch is rejected whole), `POST /hr/employees` and the
  organization member add/update routes reject illegal roles with 403
  (`invitation.roleNotAssignable` / `organization.roleNotAssignable`).
  `OrganizationService.addMember`/`updateMemberRole` take a
  `TMemberAssignmentContext` from the controller and pass the target member's
  current roles, so keeping an existing grant is not an escalation while
  creating one above the caller's tier is.

**Member-edit page (follow-up request).** `$organizationId.members.$memberId.edit.tsx`
rendered every `erpRoleNames` checkbox including `owner`, and the backend
`updateMemberRole` checked nothing but last-owner. The checkboxes now render
`useAssignableOrgRoles(organizationId, currentRoles)`; roles the caller cannot
change are listed in a hint (`memberEdit.rolesLocked`) instead of silently
vanishing, because they are still part of the member's row.

**Permanent/temporary switch (requirement 4).** `@ims-erp/ui/components/switch`
is mounted once above the dialog's tabs, so all three input modes agree:
`permanent` (default) vs `contract`. The value travels as
`employmentType` through `TInviteInput`, `invitationInputBase`,
`orgInvitationRowSchema` and into `EmployeeInviteService.defaultProfile`. The
vocabulary lives in `packages/common/src/hr/employment.ts`
(`employmentTypeNames` + labels), and the bulk template gained an
`employmentType` column (`INVITE_SHEET_HEADERS`), with per-row validation; an
empty cell falls back to the switch. `invite.fileHint` (en + id) lists the new
column.

**Employee bugs found while wiring the switch.**
- `EmployeeInviteService.defaultProfile` never set `email`, so every
  invite-created employee had `email = NULL`: the duplicate-email guard
  (`employees.findByEmail`) never fired, employee search never matched, and the
  detail card rendered `—`. Fixed (`email: row.email`).
- `components/hr/employee-form.tsx` never sent `organizationId`, so
  `EmployeeService.create` treated every submission as a company-level
  creation and rejected org HR with `CompanyEmployeeForbiddenError`. It now
  sends the active organization.

**Verification (executed 2026-11-21).**
- `packages/common`: `bun run build` clean; `bun test` 25 pass (13 new in
  `test/grantable-roles.test.ts`, 6 new/updated in `test/invite-sheet.test.ts`).
- `apps/backend`: `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; `bun test` 1251 pass / 0 fail
  (new `test/unit/role-assignment.test.ts` 12 pass; 3 new cases in
  `test/unit/employee-invite.service.test.ts` covering email + employmentType).
  The run still prints the pre-existing "database ims_erp_test does not exist"
  and "chromium crashed" noise; neither fails a test.
- `apps/web-admin`: `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` clean; `bun test`
  123 pass (4 new cases in `test/unit/invite-parse.test.ts`).
- `packages/locales`: `bun test` 98 pass (parity holds for every new key in
  both `en` and `id`).
- `bun run lint` at the root: 5/5 tasks, 0 errors (15 warnings, all pre-existing
  unused imports in untouched files).
- **Live smoke test** (`apps/backend/scripts/smoke-role-ladder.ts`, new) against
  the dev server on :3001 and the seeded database — **12/12 passed**:
  - owner caller: `owner` rejected on `/admin/invitations`, on
    `/organizations/:id/invitations` and on `/human-resources/employees`
    (all 403); a legal `member` + `contract` invite returns 201 and its
    employee row comes back with `email` set and `employmentType=contract`
    (the two employee bugs, proved fixed end to end);
  - org admin: `admin` -> 403, `hr` -> 201;
  - org HR: `admin`, `hr` and `owner` -> 403, `member` -> 201;
  - org admin promoting a member to `admin` via
    `PATCH /organizations/:id/members/:memberId` -> 403
    (`Role not assignable: admin`);
  - an application-level invite (no organization) -> 201.
- Not browser-verified: the dialog, the switch and the member-edit page were
  verified by typecheck, unit tests, lint and the live API only. The seeded
  database was left untouched (the first draft of the smoke script promoted a
  seeded account to owner; it was restored and the script no longer mutates
  roles).

No migration: `hr.employees.employment_type` already existed with its check
constraint, and `employmentType` is optional on every payload, so older clients
keep working.

## 2026-11-20 - docs.dbml and Drizzle brought into agreement: ADR-0014 enforced on 61 columns, parity check strengthened

- Finding: `validate-dbml.ts` check 5 only proved that every Drizzle table and column *name* exists in `docs.dbml`; "drizzle parity drift: 0" said nothing about nullability or types. A both-directions comparison found 185 nullability and 3 type differences. 61 of them were cross-module id columns declared `NOT NULL` in Drizzle (all `organization_id` of finance/tax/payment/sale/inventory tables, `sale.quotations.customer_id`, `sale.orders.customer_id`, `delivery_notes.warehouse_id`, `procurement.purchase_orders.supplier_company_id`, `*.product_id` lines, `project.projects.order_id/customer_id/pic_user_id`, `ticket.tickets.customer_id`, `audit.audit_logs.actor_user_id`, `notification.push_notifications.user_id`, ...), which ADR-0014 and the AGENTS.md hard rule forbid. The earlier note of "about ten" in the docs sync entry under-reported this.
- Decision (owner): follow ADR-0014 with no exception, including `organization_id` on finance, tax and payment (nullable; the service writes the caller's active organization). `updated_at` follows Drizzle in `docs.dbml` (124 columns `[not null]`); `auth.users.deleted_at` and `auth.organizations.deleted_at` are `timestamp` in `docs.dbml` (Better Auth owned); `finance.chart_of_accounts.level` is `integer`.

## 2026-11-20 - Pagination of the public catalog uses the `@ims-erp/common` contract

- Backend: `GET /inventory/public/v1/catalog/products` now answers `okPaginated(...)`: rows in `data`, the shared `TPaginationMeta` (`{ page, limit, total, totalPages }`) in `pagination`. `queryProducts` returns `TPaginationResult<TWebProduct>` (`{ meta, data }`) and clamps an out-of-range page to the last page; the query parameter `pageSize` is now `limit` (the `TPaginationRequest` name used by every staff list). `totalPages` is `ceil(total / limit)` (0 for an empty result), the repository convention.
- web-landing: `CatalogListQuery` carries `limit`; `CatalogPage` is `{ items, pagination: TPaginationMeta }` (`CatalogResult` in `lib/catalog.ts` likewise); the zod page schema validates the four `pagination` fields; the catalog results/pagination components read `pagination.total|page|totalPages`; the demo source builds the same shape. `unwrapEnvelope` (landing and portal) now returns `{ items: data, pagination }` for a paginated envelope so the contract survives unwrapping; the portal has no paginated operation yet.
- Tests: backend `product-listing.service.test.ts` asserts `meta`, landing `erp-source.test.ts` feeds a backend-shaped paginated envelope and asserts `pagination` and the `limit` query parameter, portal test asserts the paginated unwrap.
- Verified: backend `tsc` 0 errors; `bun run lint` 0 errors; `bun run test` 7/7; landing `astro check` 0 errors and build OK; portal `astro check` 0 errors and build OK. Search (`/search`) is not a page and stays a grouped result. No live run.

## 2026-11-19 - P3 step 2a: items and item categories moved from `assets` into `inventory` (ERP-0076, partial)

Backend only. Step 2 is split because the rest of `assets` is not a rename: it
sits on a changed data model (see "Design findings"). This slice is the part that
is.

- **Moved with `git mv` + compile-driven fixes** (asset -> item): contract,
  repository interface and repository, service, controller for `items` (was
  `assets.assets`) and `item_categories` (was `asset_categories`), plus the
  domain errors (`errors/item.errors.ts`: `ItemNotFoundError`,
  `ItemCategory*Error`, `ItemRuleViolationError`, `ItemTransitionError`; locale
  keys `assets.*` kept). Fields: `assetType` -> `itemKind`, `categoryId` ->
  `itemCategoryId`, `supplierId` -> `supplierCompanyId`. Tokens
  `ITEM_REPOSITORY_TOKEN`, `ITEM_CATEGORY_REPOSITORY_TOKEN`, `ITEM_SERVICE_TOKEN`,
  `ITEM_CATEGORY_SERVICE_TOKEN`, all registered in `registerInventory`.
- **URLs:** `/inventory/items` (new `/kinds` replaces `/types`, since
  `asset_types` is now the closed `ITEM_KINDS` vocabulary) and
  `/inventory/item-categories`. Permissions stay `asset:*` (RBAC rename is not
  part of this epic).
- **Boundaries fixed:** `ItemService` takes codes from
  `InventoryNumberingService` (`asset` code type, inside the transaction) and the
  `ITransactionRunner` instead of `DRIZZLE_TOKEN`; `WarehouseService` no longer
  injects `ExportedAssetService` - it counts equipment through
  `ITEM_REPOSITORY_TOKEN.countByWarehouse` (same schema).

Commands and outcomes:

```text
cd apps/backend && bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json | Select-String "^src/app/inventory"
  -> 0 lines
bun test test/unit/product.service.test.ts test/unit/stock.service.test.ts \
  test/unit/adjustment.service.test.ts -> 94 pass / 0 fail
```

Design findings for the rest of step 2 (read before starting 2b/2c):

- **Item movements are not a rename.** `assets.asset_movements` (from/to
  warehouse + storage, `moved_at`, `moved_by_user_id`, `condition`) becomes rows of
  `inventory.movements` with `item_id`, `quantity = 1`, `code` (needs
  `InventoryNumberingService`, type `stock_movement`), `warehouse_id`/`bin_id`,
  `target_warehouse_id`/`target_bin_id`, `occurred_at`, `created_by`; the old
  `transfer` type is `transfer_out`/`transfer_in` (the table forces
  `target_warehouse_id` for them) and `condition` has no column (goes into
  `notes`). Needs an `ItemMovementRepository` (create + list by item) next to the
  product-ledger `MovementRepository`; the product ledger reads must keep
  filtering on `product_id`.
- **Borrowing splits in two (Q26).** `borrowing_requests` carries draft ->
  requested -> approved/rejected/cancelled, the borrower identity (user /
  customer / guest PII) and `tool_set_id`; `borrowings` (unique per request) is
  created at **issue** and carries issued -> partially_returned -> returned ->
  closed. `borrowing_items` points at the request always and at the borrowing
  once issued; `borrowing_events` references `borrowing_id` + `borrowing_item_id`
  + `movement_id`, so `requested`/`approved`/`rejected`/`cancelled` events (no
  borrowing yet) need either a borrowing row or a relaxed FK - **to decide in
  the grill pass before coding** (proposed: events of the request half are
  recorded on the request's own timeline, i.e. `docs.dbml` gets
  `borrowing_request_events`, or `borrowing_events.borrowing_id` becomes
  nullable with a `borrowing_request_id`).
- `AssetOperationsService` (1154 lines) mixes custody sync, movements,
  conditions, maintenance, depreciation, disposal, documents and tool sets; the
  plan splits it into `MaintenanceService`, `DisposalService`, tool-set and
  document services. Depreciation leaves for `finance` (P5).

Not done: borrowing (requests, borrowings, items, events), maintenance,
condition checks, disposals, documents, tool sets, item movements; removal of
`assets` (it now has dangling imports to the moved files and stays red) and
`catalog`; `ExportedInventoryService`; frontend. `docs/database/` reviewed and
unchanged except the open event-table question above (no edit yet).

**Next executable task:** ERP-0076 step 2b - decide the borrowing-event model
(grill), then `ItemMovementRepository`, `ItemOperationsService` split, borrowing
request/borrowing services, tool sets, maintenance, disposal.

## 2026-11-19 - P1/P2 closed on the backend: company, user, portal -> customer, leads -> project (ERP-0072/0073/0074)

"finish P2 before P3" and "backend only for P3", so this step closes the P1/P2
leftovers.

  with cache-aside, `CompanyAddressRepository`, `CompanyContactRepository`,
  `CompanySettingRepository`); the old 348-line repository is gone. Profile +
  address + contacts save in one transaction through `ITransactionRunner`, and
  the profile cache is evicted after commit (`invalidate()`). New
  `ExportedCompanyService` (repository-only: `getLetterhead`, `getDocumentCode`,
  `requireDocumentCode`, `getDisplayName`). Invoice bank accounts are no longer
  part of the contract (finance, P5); controller prefix is **`/companies`**.
- **user (ERP-0072).** `role.schema` imports -> `auth.schema`; invitation insert
  now sets `createdAt/updatedAt`. The portal parts (`PortalAccountService`,
  controller, `portal-identity.repository`, mailer) left the module; new
  `ExportedUserService` over `IUserAccountGateway` (`BetterAuthUserAccountGateway`)
  gives other modules users, credentials, password tokens and sessions.
- **customer + portal (ERP-0074).** The `portal` module is deleted; its auth,
  account and data services live in `customer`. The login is the person's
  `customer.customers` row (`user_id`, `portal_role`, `portal_status`): revoke sets
  `portal_status = revoked` and frees `user_id`; `PortalContext` is now
  `{ userId, customerId (person), companyId | null, role, user, accessToken }`
  (no `identityId` / `contactId`); portal reads are scoped by
  `companyId ?? customerId`. URLs: `/customers/portal/v1[/auth]`,
  `/admin/customers/portal-accounts`. Better Auth's portal sign-in gate
  (`session.auth.ts`) reads `customer.customers`. New locale key
  `portal.noCompany` (en + id).
- **leads (Q12, moved early from P6).** `crm` is deleted. Leads, activities,
  attachments, the follow-up queue/worker and the website inquiry API now live in
  `src/app/project/` (`/projects/leads`; the public inquiry URL stays `/public/v1`
  until the Q34 alias cut-over, P8). One repository per table
  (`lead`, `lead-activity`, `lead-attachment`, `code-numbering`); website
  references are numbered in `project.code_numberings` through
  `ProjectNumberingService` in the same transaction as the lead (the `web_*` code
  types moved from `sale` to `project` in `shared/numbering/domain.ts`);
  conversion goes through `CustomerService.createCustomer` / `getActiveCustomer`.
  `LEAD_OPEN_STATUSES` added to `project.schema.ts`.
- Wiring: `src/index.ts` registers `registerCustomer` + `registerProject` (portal
  and crm registrations removed); `src/app/app.ts` mounts `customerModule()` +
  `projectModule()`. Consumers in not-yet-rebuilt modules only had their
  import paths re-pointed (quotation, whatsapp, warranty, service-ticket,
  licensing, `test-app.ts`).

## 2026-11-16 - ERP-0039: official WhatsApp (Meta Cloud API) option, registration guide, robust dedupe

The owner asked about Meta WhatsApp Business, because WAHA numbers risk bans, and about how to
register; documented and built into the n8n workflow (branch `docs/m04-n8n-workflows`, PR #114).

**Workflow (`docs/integrations/n8n/`)**
- **Provider switch.** "4. Send WhatsApp" now reads `WHATSAPP_PROVIDER`:
  - `waha`: unchanged.
  - `meta`: the Cloud API. Business-initiated messages must be approved templates, so
    `POST /v23.0/<META_PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/messages` carries `type: template`, language `id`, and
    body parameters.
  - A message without a template is skipped and reported, never sent as free text.
- **Templates.** "3. Compose messages" now gives every message both forms: the free text and a
  template name with its parameters (new lines flattened, as Meta refuses them).
- **Template tooling.**
  - `meta-templates.json`: 15 Indonesian Utility templates.
  - `create-meta-templates.ts`: submits them to the WABA.
  - `check-meta-templates.ts`: runs the compose code for every topic and change, and checks
    template names and parameter counts.
  - `samples.ts`: holds the sample events shared by the scripts.
- **Dedupe fix found by testing.**
  - The problem: workflow static data is loaded when an execution starts and saved when it
    ends, after the ERP already has its answer. An event re-sent right away got through: 1 of 3
    repeats, and the Meta run's third retry attempt.
  - The fix: dedupe now uses an n8n data table `erp_processed_events`. Node "2a" creates it if
    missing (`createIfNotExists`), "2b" looks the id up, and "5a" upserts it only after the
    sends succeeded, all before the answer.

**Docs**
- New `docs/user-guide/whatsapp-business-meta.id.md` / `.en.md`:
  - WAHA vs Meta;
  - what to prepare (legal data, documents, a dedicated number not on the app, payment method,
    display name);
  - step-by-step registration (portfolio, app, WABA, number, business verification, Billing Hub,
    System User token);
  - template rules and the catalog, limits (250 → 2,000 …, per portfolio), cost model (per
    message since 2025-07-01, service charged from 2026-10-01) with a rate warning, opt-in;
  - n8n config, and a migration plan.
- These facts were checked against Meta's official docs on 2026-11-16 (pricing, messaging limits,
  get started, templates, webhook endpoint). The Indonesian per-message rates come only from
  third-party sources that disagree, so the guide says to verify them.
- `n8n-workflows.*.md`: the node table (data table, provider) and env vars were updated.
- `whatsapp-n8n-setup.*.md` warn about WAHA bans and link the Meta guide.

**Verification on a real n8n 2.47.7, with a mock WAHA + Graph API on :3999**
- `check-meta-templates.ts`: 34 messages against 15 templates, `OK`.
- **Meta mode.**
  - `send-test-event.ts all` returned 10× 200, giving 13 Graph calls with the right URL
    (`/v23.0/<id>/messages`), Bearer token and template payloads.
  - The extra changes (approved / shipped / received / overdue) also passed, including the
    supplier template with 6 parameters.
  - Meta answering 500 → webhook 500 → the retry succeeds → the next try is "duplicate".
- **Dedupe:** 6/6 immediate repeats were detected (before the fix: 1/3 got through), and a bad
  signature returned 401.
- **WAHA mode regression:** all 10 topics returned 200 with 15 WAHA calls, and a repeat was
  "duplicate".
- `create-meta-templates.ts` against the mock: 15 submissions to `/<WABA>/message_templates`.

## 2026-11-16 - ERP-0039: importable n8n workflow for every ERP event, tested on a real n8n

  all topics.
  - Nodes: webhook `erp-events` → verify the HMAC signature (±10 minutes
    replay window) → skip duplicates (workflow static data) → compose

  switch (default off).

  - The PDF is made in a queue, never in the "send" request.
  - The render view is public, but it needs a 2-minute HMAC token per
    quotation (`APP_SECRET`).
  - The PDF is stored on the quotation's registry document (ERP-0044), so the
    document screen lists it and can revoke the link.
  - Three attempts; the last publishes with `pdf: null`.
  - One event per sending (dedupe key = id and `sent_at`).
